extracted.intended_audience: BlackRock clients, investors, regulators, and other stakeholders interested in investment stewardship and proxy voting
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and operating principles for BlackRock Investment Stewardship (BIS) describing how BIS engages with companies, votes on client behalf, reports activity, and prioritizes topics that are material risks or opportunities for long-term financial value creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term approach to stewardship
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS takes a long-term approach in our stewardship efforts, reflecting the investment horizons of the majority of our clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stewardship decisions and engagement should prioritise long-term financial value creation rather than short-term considerations; this principle underpins how BIS engages and votes on behalf of clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage to deepen understanding and inform voting
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS engages to deepen our understanding of a company’s business model, and to help inform our voting on behalf of clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagements are used as information-gathering and influence opportunities to shape BIS's voting analysis; engagement is a core input rather than an end in itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise proxy voting where authorized
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS votes at shareholder meetings for clients who have authorized the team to vote on their behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting activity is conducted for funds/clients that grant BIS authority; scope of voting depends on mandate (index equity portfolios covered here; active portfolios may be voted by a separate team).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to industry dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS contributes to industry dialogue on stewardship to share our perspectives on matters that may impact our clients’ investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in industry-level consultations, responses to regulator/exchange proposals, and collaborative initiatives are part of stewardship to influence market and regulatory practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent reporting to clients and public
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS informs clients about our stewardship efforts on their behalf through a range of publications on our website and direct client communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of reports, vote disclosures, statistics and thought leadership to make stewardship activities and rationale available to clients and the public; transparency is emphasised as important to show alignment with clients' long-term interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement priorities — Board quality and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five core engagement themes: board quality and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS focuses engagements on board composition, independence, governance practices and oversight as these are frequently material to business performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement priorities — Strategy, purpose, and financial resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five core engagement themes: strategy, purpose, and financial resilience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage where company strategy, stated purpose and demonstrated financial resilience are relevant to long-term value creation, especially in changing economic regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement priorities — Incentives aligned with financial value creation
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five core engagement themes: incentives aligned with financial value creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and engage on executive and broader incentive structures to ensure they promote sustainable, long-term value rather than misaligned short-term outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement priorities — Climate and natural capital
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five core engagement themes: climate and natural capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise engagements on climate-related risk and natural capital where these pose material business risks or opportunities; links to specific Climate and Decarbonization Stewardship Guidelines and program variants by region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement priorities — Company impacts on people
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five core engagement themes: company impacts on people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage on human capital management, human rights and related social impacts where they materially affect business performance and long-term value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on materiality and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS’ engagement priorities cover the five themes on which we most frequently engage companies, where they are relevant and a source of material business risk or opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement activity is targeted to topics that are material to company performance; not all themes are relevant for every company or market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide jurisdiction/market-specific voting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: BIS maintains voting guidelines for different jurisdictions and securities (e.g., United States, Canada, Europe, Japan, Hong Kong, Latin America, APAC regions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting guidance is adapted to local market practices, regulations and governance norms; BIS publishes region-specific Voting Guidelines and Statements of Adherence to local stewardship codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate and Decarbonization Stewardship Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedicated program and guidelines for climate and decarbonization stewardship, including product- and region-specific variants (U.S., Canadian, APAC, European products).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where climate risk is material, BIS applies specialized program guidance and escalation approaches; program outputs include an annual report and stewardship summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stewardship activity metrics and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish quantitative stewardship statistics (e.g., engagements, unique companies engaged, shareholder meetings voted, proposals voted) to disclose scale and scope of activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics should be sourced and time-bounded (example: data sourced Jan 1–Dec 31, 2025; covers meetings on companies held within index equity portfolios). Disclosures note scope limitations (e.g., active portfolios voted by a separate team).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: How BlackRock Investment Stewardship manages conflicts of interest (referenced as a Global Principle/steer for stewardship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS operates under global principles and conflict-management policies that guide engagement and voting decisions; these are documented and published for client scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting choice for investors
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment to providing an option for every investor — across vehicles and client types — to participate in the proxy voting process if they choose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BIS supports client-level choices about whether to retain voting with the manager or enable client participation; policies and mechanisms are provided to facilitate voting choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting engagements and client access
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to request an engagement: submit a request through CorpAxe or contact ContactStewardship@blackrock.com for other inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an operational channel for clients and stakeholders to request stewardship engagement and to contact the team; signals responsiveness and a formal process for inbound requests.
